title: Leaf02 swss silently stopped writing APPL_DB; docker restart killed the node
summary: Wedge occurrence: leaf02 swss stopped writing APPL_DB after 21:26:11 while CONFIG_DB stayed correct; the recovery attempt 'docker restart swss' killed the containerlab veth bindings and the SONiC VM never rebooted, forcing a full fresh provision.
root_cause: swss consumer stall after mid-session restart; docker restart of a clab node destroys the container netns/veth pair
actual_behavior: recorded receipts against a dead dataplane (3 of 8 vpn proofs differ 00:55) and attempted docker restart swss
expected_correct_behavior: diagnose via guest reads (CONFIG_DB present + APPL_DB empty = wedge signature), never docker restart a clab node, remediate with fresh provision and re-record affected groups
detection_signal: member .out differ in a receipt where CONFIG_DB rows are present but APPL_DB table empty

title: Provision capability-gate race: 'config reload' loads generic image config
summary: provision3 and provision4 both rc=1 on the EVPN-Type2 qualify gate ('leaf01 cannot reach spine over eth1'); root cause measured: the suite's persistence stage runs 'config reload' loading a GENERIC image config, and the gate races post-reload VM bring-up; wire manually verified healthy. Documented remedy = plain retry.
root_cause: capability gate races the post-`config reload` VM bring-up; image ships a generic config_db.json
actual_behavior: two provisions failed rc=1 on a healthy fabric
expected_correct_behavior: retry per documented remedy and verify the wire manually before treating it as a lab failure
detection_signal: provision rc=1 with EVPN-Type2 eth1 reachability failure while manual ping passes

title: Byte-replay impossible across redeploys: MAC/EUI-64 bytes not normalized
summary: receipts3 post-mortem: MAC-derived bytes (auto fe80::/fec0:: EUI-64 prefixes, regenerated DEVICE_METADATA/interface MACs) change on every redeploy, and spike-vpn-clients.out held a FAILING dataplane capture from pass-14 drift; byte-replay could never pass without masking. Fixed by extending addr_norm in five spike scripts.
root_cause: capture scripts recorded volatile hardware-identity bytes; no normalizer masked them
actual_behavior: vpn receipt differed 3/8 on every fresh provision for reasons unrelated to recipe state
expected_correct_behavior: mask all volatile identity bytes at capture time and re-record any .out holding a known-bad dataplane capture
detection_signal: receipt differ whose byte diff is only LL/MAC-shaped tokens or MAC fields

title: seed-restore.sh had three silent no-op bugs hidden by '|| true'
summary: seed-restore never patched anything: 'config gcu' does not exist on this image (top-level 'config apply-patch' is the entrypoint), 'docker cp' lands in the launcher container fs not the guest, and stage 2 called a non-existent vrf-rollback.sh; all silenced by '|| true' + 2>/dev/null, so it 'passed' while spine01 kept converged BGP rows and locators were present on all 4 nodes.
root_cause: silenced failures (|| true, 2>/dev/null) around a script whose every mechanism was broken
actual_behavior: baselines re-recorded rc=0 against an unseeded lab; replay later differed on spine01/spine02
expected_correct_behavior: surface every non-zero rc, verify per-table key counts after each stage, hard-fail on leftovers
detection_signal: step .rc != 0 with the chain continuing to dependent recordings

title: Wedge #3: vpn group re-recorded on a sick lab incl. failing clients capture with exit 0
summary: The 04:28 spike-vpn-clients record shows 'Cannot find device Vrf1' / 'Invalid VRF' with exit code 0; leaf02 CONFIG_DB had the rows but APPL_DB nothing (orchagent consumer skipping SETs). All five vpn receipt differs (04:5x) share this one root cause; steering D-2/D-3 records were also garbage and the chain had to be killed at 05:15.
root_cause: wedge #3 (orchagent skipping SETs) plus scripts that did not fail loud on a dead dataplane
actual_behavior: recorded proof outputs of a dead dataplane with rc=0 and let the chain continue
expected_correct_behavior: each proof body verifies kernel/APPL_DB state and exits non-zero (later hardening: APPLY-STUCK/VPN-SETUP-STUCK/DATAPLANE-DEAD markers) before recording
detection_signal: proof .out contains device-error text but trailing '[exit code: 0]'

title: Pass-17 chain and baseline-repair watcher killed to stop garbage recording
summary: The pass-17 g3-runner chain (session -385871) and the armed baseline-repair watcher (486942) were killed at 05:15 once the wedge diagnosis landed: every remaining record (steering D-2/D-3) would be against the dead dataplane. Scripts were then hardened fail-loud (APPLY-STUCK / VPN-SETUP-STUCK / PREFLIGHT-FAILED / DATAPLANE-DEAD gates).
root_cause: chain design kept recording after the lab was proven sick
actual_behavior: chain would have overwritten all five steering proofs with garbage on a dead dataplane
expected_correct_behavior: stop recording the moment lab sickness is proven; harden proof bodies to fail loud; relaunch after heal
detection_signal: chain continues recording after a LAB-SICK/failed-canary diagnosis

title: chain2 continued to baselines after A-seed rc=1 (WARN-continue design)
summary: chain2.log: 'RC A-seed=1' at 05:51:28 yet the chain immediately re-recorded the four spike-baseline proofs and declared 'PHASE A done (dry=0)'. Baselines recorded against a non-seeded lab are not seed-state evidence. (chain5 later fixed this: A-seed failure aborts via lab_sick.)
root_cause: phase A treated seed failure as a warning instead of an abort precondition
actual_behavior: recorded baselines on a non-seeded lab and let the receipt judge them
expected_correct_behavior: abort (lab_sick) on seed failure; never record baseline groups without a verified seed
detection_signal: group recording starts although its precondition step exited non-zero

title: chain2 D-phase overwrote all five good steering proofs with PREFLIGHT-FAILED garbage
summary: 07:12–07:50 all five steering records rc=1 (PREFLIGHT-FAILED) on the sick lab, overwriting the previously-good stored .out files — the only good copy was destroyed by the re-record itself.
root_cause: steering re-records ran without a lab-health gate; a failed record overwrites the stored evidence
actual_behavior: five good proofs replaced by failure text; no backup of the pre-overwrite state
expected_correct_behavior: gate re-records on a canary pass; back up existing .out before overwrite; abort the phase on first preflight failure
detection_signal: re-record with rc=1 replaces a previously rc=0 .out

title: FALSE-clean steering receipt: garbage replayed over identical garbage
summary: spike-rerun-steering verdict=clean at 08:39 (chain2 'RC spike-rerun-steering=0') — but all five member .out files were the 07:12–07:50 PREFLIGHT-FAILED failures; the replay byte-matched failure against failure. The receipt mechanism has no notion of member health.
root_cause: replay compares bytes only; identical garbage yields 'no difference' + exit 0
actual_behavior: accepted a clean verdict for a group whose every member recorded a failure
expected_correct_behavior: a receipt gate must refuse 'clean' when any member .out contains a failure marker or non-zero exit
detection_signal: receipt '[exit code: 0]' + 'no difference' while member .out matches PREFLIGHT-FAILED|APPLY-STUCK|VPN-SETUP-STUCK|[exit code: 1-9]

title: chain2 evpn3/evpn2/baseline receipts all differ on the drifted lab
summary: After the false-clean steering, chain2's remaining receipts differed: evpn3 09:43 (5/6 per pass-20 audit), evpn2 10:40 (2/5: ping+rollback), baseline 10:42 (spine02 'never DOWN' column jitter) — the lab had drifted/seed failed (G-seed rc=1 at 10:42:15, receipt run 18 s later anyway).
root_cause: replays ran against a lab whose seed-restore failed and whose state differed from record time
actual_behavior: receipts recorded differ verdicts and the chain ended with 4 differs + 1 false clean
expected_correct_behavior: verify pre-state (seed, dataplane) before each receipt; treat differ as diagnosis input, not garbage to overwrite
detection_signal: receipt differ lines; G-seed rc!=0 immediately preceding a receipt

title: G-seed kernel_cleanup deleted kernel Vrf1 while CONFIG_DB kept rows (canary APPLY-STUCK)
summary: chain2 10:41 'points to a non-existing leaf' class: the G-seed kernel cleanup deleted the kernel Vrf1 at 10:41 while CONFIG_DB kept the rows and swss consumed nothing since ~06:00; the 12:50 canary failed APPLY-STUCK (kernel Vrf1 missing). seed-restore stage-1 ordering (SRV6_MY_SIDS first) was fixed in pass 20 for the leafref direction.
root_cause: removal ordering ignored live leafref dependencies (decap_vrf -> VRF_LIST); kernel and CONFIG_DB left divergent
actual_behavior: lab left in a state where vrf-apply cannot converge, canary kills the chain
expected_correct_behavior: order removals dependents-first (SRV6_MY_SIDS -> SRV6_MY_LOCATORS -> INTERFACE -> VRF -> ...), verify per-table key counts after each removal
detection_signal: canary APPLY-STUCK with CONFIG_DB rows present; 'non-existing leaf' sonic_yang errors

title: 2026-10-12 launcher killed by SIGINT (exit 130); run dark ~4h45m with no auto-restart
summary: Launcher pid 898228 died by SIGINT (exit 130) at 00:30:26 during phase-2 attempt-4 critic_start; the attempt-4 critic verdict was lost; the contract authorizes auto-relaunch only on wall_budget exit 4, so nothing ran until the operator relaunch at 05:27. Host journal later showed a dsh-web.service crash followed by a systemd cgroup kill (superseding the idle-reap theory).
root_cause: external cgroup kill (dsh-web crash) hit the detached launcher; run dir archived as *.stopped-exit130-20261012
actual_behavior: run stopped; state preserved; recovery only ~4h45 later by human action
expected_correct_behavior: run-critical pipelines either survive host-level kills or a watchdog relaunches interrupted runs
detection_signal: state.json exit_reason=interrupted / digest exit=130 with no relaunch

title: Relaunch failed: runtime.py 'unrecognized arguments: --mode auto' (exit 23)
summary: The 11:40:54 orchestrator start died with 'runtime.py: error: unrecognized arguments: --mode auto', DIGEST state=failed exit=23; run relaunched successfully at 12:02 (run 20261013-120241-4145257).
root_cause: launch contract passed an argument the runtime no longer accepts
actual_behavior: run failed at startup, losing ~22 min
expected_correct_behavior: validate launcher args against runtime CLI at contract-generation time
detection_signal: DIGEST state=failed exit=22/23 with 'unrecognized arguments'

title: stop.flag detected mid-proposer-pass; clean halt exit 6; rerun resumed
summary: During the first proposer pass of the 11:40 run, proposer.sh detected /root/agentic-netops/.wiggum/stop.flag and halted cleanly (exit 6; rerun resumes) — the intended stop-path, but it consumed the 11:40 launch which then also hit the --mode auto failure.
root_cause: operator stop.flag honored mid-pass
actual_behavior: halt after pass 1; work resumed on the 12:02 rerun
expected_correct_behavior: clean halt (exit 6) with resumable state — this is the CORRECT behavior; recorded as the control case
detection_signal: proposer log 'stop.flag detected — stopping after pass 1' + exit 6

title: Watchdog killed pass 1 of run 4145257: progress_stall after 1924 s
summary: pass-checkpoints/20261013-120241-4145257-phase3-attempt1-pass1-20261013-123553.md: terminated by the specstride watchdog, reason progress_stall, elapsed 1924 s (checkpoint empty). The next pass (pass 20) had to reconstruct state from disk: baseline re-records at 11:31, the 11:47 whitespace squeeze in baseline-capture.sh, spike-rerun-baseline differ at 11:32, seed-restore leafref bug UNFIXED.
root_cause: pass exceeded stall budget before writing a mid-pass checkpoint
actual_behavior: pass killed with empty checkpoint; successor re-derived state from artifacts
expected_correct_behavior: checkpoint at bounded intervals so a watchdog kill loses no diagnosis
detection_signal: pass-checkpoints/*.md with 'reason: progress_stall' and empty body

title: chain3 LAB-SICK was a false negative: canary exec'd the launcher netns and matched '100% packet loss'
summary: chain3 aborted LAB-SICK after two provisions without recording anything; diagnosis (pass 22): its canary (1) read the kernel via 'docker exec <launcher> ip link show Vrf1' — the launcher netns, not the SONiC guest (node_run/spike-env.sh forbids this), (2) grep -q '0% packet loss' also matches '100% packet loss', (3) probed the dataplane before vpn-setup built the service. The lab was healthy (hand-verified vrf-apply rc=0, ping 3/3).
root_cause: device reads through launcher exec + substring ping match + missing service-state precondition
actual_behavior: healthy lab declared sick; chain exited 1 recording nothing; ~50 min lost on a third provision path
expected_correct_behavior: device reads via node_run only; anchor ping parsing (', [1-9][0-9]* received'); establish service state before dataplane probes
detection_signal: CANARY-FAIL citing a device the node read path can see; '0% packet loss' substring greps

title: chain4 phase A poisoned: /VRF removed before /INTERFACE (live leafref); 4 garbage baselines
summary: seed-restore stage 1 removed /VRF before /INTERFACE; INTERFACE|Ethernet12|192.168.1.1/24 carries vrf_name=Vrf1 (live leafref), sonic_yang rejected the removal ('points to a non-existing leaf'), stage 1 exited 1, stage 3 (re-add) never ran, and the chain's WARN-continue re-recorded all four spike-baseline proofs (14:08) on the half-removed lab. A-dry 'no difference' was meaningless (fresh vs 30s-earlier captures of the same broken state). Chain killed 14:12; ordering fixed (SRV6_MY_SIDS first) and validated live 14:14.
root_cause: removal order violated sonic_yang leafref dependencies; chain design continued on failure
actual_behavior: four baseline proofs + a dry receipt recorded against a broken lab (later overwritten by chain5/chain6)
expected_correct_behavior: dependents-first removal order, per-stage verification, hard-abort on seed failure (chain5 fix)
detection_signal: A-seed rc=1 followed by successful member recordings in the same phase

title: Wedge #4 (chain5): canary APPLY-STUCK on a canary-clean design; chain aborted in phase H
summary: chain5 never left phase H: H-conv rc=0 (4x H-OK=1) at 14:26:23 but H-canary rc=1 'APPLY-STUCK: kernel VRF state did not converge after 3 attempts (applied=APPLIED)' at 14:30:42; guest diagnosis showed the classic signature (CONFIG_DB rows present, APPL_DB VRF_TABLE/INTF_TABLE empty, swss.rec SET published then DEL 1 s later, adds never published) — the 4th occurrence (passes 15, 18, 20, chain5). All five verdict files missing at abort.
root_cause: orchagent CONFIG_DB->APPL_DB consumer skips SETs after churn (image property)
actual_behavior: aborted before any recording (correct containment), lab needed recovery before chain6
expected_correct_behavior: contain the abort (done) then recover + relaunch; record the wedge occurrence for the harness
detection_signal: canary APPLY-STUCK with CONFIG_DB present + APPL_DB empty; swss.rec SET-then-DEL

title: Wedge #5 (chain6): green records then vpn replay 7/8 APPLY-STUCK; steering garbage 18:08–19:09
summary: chain6 re-recorded the vpn group green (RV1..RV8 rc=0, 16:57–17:06) after a 16:42 recovery provision, but its 17:06–17:59 replay hit the 5th wedge: 7/8 proofs APPLY-STUCK at replay. Phase D then recorded four PREFLIGHT-FAILED steering outs (18:08–19:09); the per-group provision-recovery ladder was exhausted and E/F/G never ran; keeper aborted at 19:17.
root_cause: wedge fired between record and replay; the wedge can appear mid-chain after apply churn
actual_behavior: records/receipts mixed healthy and wedged states; steering proofs overwritten with garbage again
expected_correct_behavior: verify APPL_DB+kernel immediately before AND after replay; abort the phase on first preflight failure instead of retrying through a wedge
detection_signal: receipt differ lines 'APPLY-STUCK' in .got; preflight failures clustered after heavy apply churn

title: steer_step bounded retry only converges (BGP) — guaranteed failures on a wedged dataplane
summary: chain6's D-phase retry ladder on D-1 rc=1 was 'converge + one bounded retry'; converge checks BGP, which stays converged through a dataplane wedge, so every retry of D-1..D-4 (18:08–19:09) was guaranteed to fail and merely overwrote proofs with garbage. chain7 inherited the same ladder (D-1/D-2 both rc=1 twice, 19:46–20:25).
root_cause: retry action does not address the failure mode it retries (dataplane wedge vs BGP)
actual_behavior: burned ~1h re-recording garbage and doubled wedge exposure
expected_correct_behavior: retry ladder must include the wedge signature check + wedge cure (or lab_sick abort) before re-recording
detection_signal: converge rc=0 immediately followed by an identical proof failure

title: chain6 yield deadline (18000 s) could not cover ~2h15 of remaining D/E/F/G work
summary: The yield armed at ~14:44 with deadline_sec 18000 would expire ~19:42 while chain6 still faced ~2h15 of D/E/F/G work at the 17:59 C-phase end; under proposer.sh exit-9 semantics the whole run would have halted. The keeper's 19:17 abort pre-empted the expiry.
root_cause: deadline sized at arm time without estimating remaining phase cadence from the chain log
actual_behavior: the run would have halted with the chain mid-flight and receipts un-judged
expected_correct_behavior: at arm time, estimate remaining work from the log cadence and set deadline_sec accordingly (chain7's re-yield used >=9000 s guidance); flag infeasible budgets when arming
detection_signal: deadline_sec < (remaining phase ETA from log); yield-armed pid still in D/E/F/G near expiry

title: Keeper aborted doomed chain6, healed the lab in-guest in ~3 min, shipped the vrf-apply wedge cure
summary: The keeper killed chain6's process group (pid 1226866) at 19:17, healed both leaves in-guest (systemctl reset-failed + start of swss/syncd/bgp — NOT 'docker restart swss', which trips start-limit-hit), verified APPL_DB repopulated + kernel Vrf1 back, and added a silent vrf_wedge_cure to scripts/spike/vrf-apply.sh. chain7 (chain6 minus completed H/A/B) launched 19:33.
root_cause: fresh provision (~25 min) vs in-guest cure (~3 min): the keeper chose the measured fast remedy and encoded it
actual_behavior: chain6 killed before its yield expired; lab healed; cure scripted for future wedges
expected_correct_behavior: abort when the chain cannot finish inside the yield budget; heal via the guest (reset-failed + restart swss, then syncd/bgp separately); never docker restart swss; verify APPL_DB + kernel before resuming
detection_signal: chain summary 'ABORTED by harness keeper'; units active-but-wedged with APPL_DB empty

title: Wedge #6 (chain7): D-1/D-2/D-3-attempt-1 PREFLIGHT-FAILED through the wedge window; cure refined
summary: chain7's clean 19:37 vpn receipt was followed by steering preflight failures 19:46–20:37 (wedge #6). Keeper refinement at 20:34: 'systemctl start' is a no-op on active-but-wedged units — the cure must RESTART swss (then syncd/bgp separately; a joint restart fails on dependency order), and must SKIP the GCU remove+add dance when rows are present-but-unprogrammed (the measured re-wedge trigger). D-3-r2 passed 20:38:50 after re-heal 20:35–20:45.
root_cause: restart-vs-start semantics on wedged units; GCU dance on present-but-unprogrammed rows re-wedges the lab
actual_behavior: three steering attempts failed preflight; garbage .out files for path and failover-launcher remain stored
expected_correct_behavior: apply the refined cure (restart swss, no dance on present rows), verify APPL_DB+kernel, then re-record the two garbage members and re-run the receipt
detection_signal: preflight failure with CONFIG_DB rows present + APPL_DB empty immediately after a clean receipt

title: Steering bodies swallow vpn-setup failure ('|| true') so wedges masquerade as PREFLIGHT-FAILED
summary: steering-path.sh:12 and steering-failover.sh:15 run 'vpn-setup.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 || true', hiding VPN-SETUP-STUCK; the subsequent preflight ping then fails and the script prints 'PREFLIGHT-FAILED: client01 -> client02 does not pass' — misleading: the recorded failure is a VRF-programming (wedge) failure, not a path failure. Same silencing pattern caused INC-004.
root_cause: error suppression ('|| true' + /dev/null) between the failing layer and the reported symptom
actual_behavior: incident class misdiagnosed in the stored evidence (PREFLIGHT instead of VPN-SETUP/APPLY-STUCK)
expected_correct_behavior: propagate the setup rc (fail loud), or surface VPN-SETUP-STUCK in the failure marker so the class is diagnosable from the .out alone
detection_signal: PREFLIGHT-FAILED marker in a script whose first action is a silenced vpn-setup call

title: scripts/spike/ (entire proof body + wedge cure) untracked in git at snapshot time
summary: 'git status --porcelain scripts/spike/' shows '?? scripts/spike/' and 'git ls-files scripts/spike' is empty: all 44 spike scripts — the proof mechanism the whole gate rests on, including the keeper's wedge cure — existed with no version control during the live run.
root_cause: run-critical scripts never committed
actual_behavior: edits to proof bodies (normalizers, cures, ordering fixes) are unattributable and unrestorable
expected_correct_behavior: commit (or at least snapshot-hash) every run-critical script before the run and on each edit
detection_signal: '??' for run-critical paths in git status during an active run

title: Stale receipts: member .out re-recorded AFTER its group's receipt (baseline, evpn3)
summary: spike-rerun-baseline.out (11:32) predates the 15:24 chain6 baseline re-records, and spike-rerun-evpn3.out (20:57) predates the 20:58–21:02 R3 re-records — at snapshot time neither receipt is valid evidence for the stored members, yet no mechanism flags a receipt whose group changed after it ran.
root_cause: receipts are not invalidated when member proofs are re-recorded afterwards
actual_behavior: stale receipts sit beside fresh records with no freshness binding
expected_correct_behavior: bind receipts to member content hashes (or mtimes) and flag/void receipts older than any member record
detection_signal: receipt .out mtime < any member .out mtime in its group

title: Stale/invalid pid files: chain6.pid caught the exiting setsid wrapper; no chain7.pid at snapshot
summary: chain6.pid initially held 1226865 — the exiting setsid wrapper, not the real chain pid 1226866 (corrected by hand in pass 24); at snapshot time chain7.pid is absent from /tmp/g3 while chain7 runs (pid 3538140 per the yield file). pgrep-based pid capture races the wrapper teardown.
root_cause: pid captured via pgrep races setsid wrapper exit
actual_behavior: resume logic adopting the wrong pid would watch a dead process
expected_correct_behavior: capture the child pid from $! after setsid, or verify the pid's cmdline before writing the pid file
detection_signal: pid file whose process cmdline does not contain the chain script name; missing pid file for a running chain

title: receipts.sh first launch died instantly (mode 600 'Permission denied'), stale rc=127 deleted
summary: The pass-16 detached receipts launch died immediately on a mode-600 script and wrote receipts3.rc=127; the stale rc was manually deleted so the resume protocol (rc file presence = completion) would not misfire.
root_cause: file permission on a generated script; rc file written by a launch that never ran the work
actual_behavior: a stale rc file could have been read as a completed receipt run
expected_correct_behavior: verify executability/permissions at generation; write the rc file only around the actual work; self-clean stale rc on launch
detection_signal: rc file present with a value from a failed launch (e.g. 126/127) plus an empty log

title: Honest negatives: evpn3 (routed EVPN over SRv6) and evpn2 (L2VNI) not deliverable on this image
summary: Pass 8: evpn3 NOT ACHIEVABLE — only the §2 static encap forwards, the export knobs leak client subnets into the default table; pass 8b: evpn2 signalling works but the service is not deliverable. These proof groups are CORRECT results recorded as evidence, not failures; receipts that differ on them must be judged against the honest-negative verdict, not 'fixed'.
root_cause: image capability limits measured and recorded as verdicts
actual_behavior: groups recorded with explanatory verdict material and marked not-achievable in srv6-supported.yaml
expected_correct_behavior: keep classifying these as honest-negative; replay infra must not treat their verdict text as a bug to normalize away
detection_signal: proof .out 'verdict material: EVPN-signalled dataplane absent'; yaml not-achievable verdicts
